definition: The efficiency and effectiveness with which individuals or teams complete tasks and achieve goals.
extendedDefinition: Productivity measures how efficiently individuals and teams convert effort into output, and in software terms it is often the first benefit evaluated in a buying decision. Modern productivity tools aim to reduce context switching, automate repetitive work, and centralize information so that people spend more time on high-value tasks. Measuring productivity fairly requires a baseline: tracking task completion, turnaround times, and time-to-value before and after a tool rollout reveals whether the investment actually helped. Leaders should be cautious with simplistic metrics like hours logged, which can reward visibility instead of results. The most reliable gains come when tools fit the team's existing workflow rather than forcing a new process. For software buyers, productivity claims should be validated with pilot results and measurable before-and-after comparisons.
